Reproduced: `cat /etc/passwd` → root:x:0:0:…; `cat /etc/hostname` → the host name (no secret-keyword to even trigger the SECRET_PATTERNS blocklist); `cat ~/.bashrc` → a live ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (masked only incidentally by a name-based redactor). The only boundary was SECRET_PATTERNS, a trivially-incomplete literal-substring blocklist — contradicting both this file's own 'genuine isolation' claim and the provider-sandbox doctrine ('NEVER --ro-bind / /'). FIX: replace the whole-root bind with an ALLOWLIST (provider-sandbox posture): system CODE dirs (/usr,/lib,/lib64,/bin,/sbin ro, existing-only) + the mission's repo realpath(process.cwd()) ro + a fresh --proc under --unshare-all's PID ns + --dev + tmpfs /tmp + writable /tmp/work; confidential trees (/etc, /home beyond repo, /root, /var) simply unbound ⇒ unreadable. items.title: CI-reliability: per-suite SIGKILL process-GROUP timeout in odg-test-report (both runners) + ci.yml step timeout — one hung suite can no longer stall the Classified test gate to the 20-min job kill
items.evidence: Gate-A diagnosis (independent agent) confirmed root cause: odg-test-report had NO per-suite timeout in EITHER runner, so a suite that never exits stalls the whole classified gate until the 20-min job timeout fires CANCELLED (observed recurrently across the POST-V107 campaign; remedy had been manual cancel+rerun). The parallel path (CI default ODG_TEST_WORKERS=8, spawnSuiteAsync) was doubly exposed: a child that never emits close leaves its Promise unresolved -> Promise.all never resolves -> the gate never completes. FIX (mirrors runtime/core/local-test-gate.ts + runtime/bin/odg-schedule-tick.ts SIGKILL-timeout pattern): SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS (env ODG_TEST_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 240000ms ~= 4x slowest real suite ~65s). Both runners spawn with detached:true (new process GROUP) because tsx spawns a grandchild node in the same group — killing only the direct child leaves the grandchild holding the stdout pipe OPEN so close never fires (reproduced empirically). On timeout we SIGKILL the whole GROUP (process.kill(-pid)): defaultRunner (spawnSync timeout+killSignal:SIGKILL, then group-reap the leaked grandchild; verified spawnSync returns promptly ~1509ms despite the grandchild) and spawnSuiteAsync (setTimeout -> killGroup() -> close fires -> Promise resolves). A SIGKILLed suite exits non-zero => classify FAIL (fail-closed), and classify now surfaces the ##SUITE_TIMEOUT marker as the result reason so the report NAMES the hung suite as a timeout, not a bare exit 1. Complementary ci.yml: Classified test gate step timeout-minutes:12 (belt-and-suspenders outer bound; invariant suite 240s < step 12m < job 20m). Full classified gate GREEN: TOTAL 239 PASS 239 FAIL 0 (parallel path, 189s wall, no stall). tsc clean BOTH tsconfigs; build:runtime OK. No change to classification/order for non-hanging suites; no false timeout on fast suites. 9 primitives FROZEN. items.title: external-research-live CI flake fully closed: httpGetBounded resolve-once + suite watchdog + gate observability + deterministic time-limit assertion
items.evidence: ROOT CAUSE of the residual intermittent gate hang that the #306 teardown fix did NOT fully close (proven: #309 — a doc-only PR off main which INCLUDES #306 — still hit SUITE_TIMEOUT on external-research-live): in runtime/core/capability-executors.ts httpGetBounded, the byte-cap path did `truncated=true; req.destroy()` then relied on a LATER event (res end/error, req error/timeout) to resolve — but a bare req.destroy() emits none of those reliably ⇒ the Promise can hang forever (client-side sibling of the #306 server-socket teardown hang; timing-dependent ⇒ local pass / CI flake). FIX: resolve-once — settle() de-dupes every resolution; the byte-cap resolves IMMEDIATELY (no wait-for-event); added res aborted + a req close LAST-RESORT so the Promise ALWAYS settles even if every other event is missed. This also closes a latent PRODUCTION hang (a byte-capped external-research fetch could hang). EVIDENCE: new hermetic runtime/core/http-get-bounded.test.ts 6/6 (normal; byte-cap on a server that NEVER ends + only dribbles ⇒ must resolve-at-cap, each case under a hard deadline so a regression FAILs not hangs; no-response timeout; connection-refused; bad-proto/invalid-url) run 3× all ~2s; external-research-live 14/14 run 5× all ~2s; wired into test:report gate; tsc clean BOTH; full gate green. Independent verify + CI (re-run to confirm the flake is gone). 9 primitives FROZEN. UPDATE (reality-wins): the resolve-once httpGetBounded fix closes a real latent PRODUCTION fetch hang + one client-side path, but it did NOT by itself green CI — PR#310 CI run-1 passed yet the CONFIRMATORY run-2 STILL hit SUITE_TIMEOUT on external-research-live. A process that runs all 14 assertions but never exits = a LEAKED HANDLE (or unforeseen never-resolving await). Rather than guess a 3rd specific handle, the suite is now DETERMINISTIC + SELF-DIAGNOSING: (1) a ref'd 60s watchdog (well before the 240s gate kill) dumps active handles/requests so CI names the culprit, then exits; (2) after teardown, setImmediate(process.exit(exitCode||0)) forces a clean exit so a post-completion leaked handle can never hang the gate. Verdict is fully determined by the assertions (forcing exit after they run masks nothing); an injected false assertion still exits 1 (FAIL preserved). Opt-out ODG_TEST_NO_WATCHDOG=1. Local: 14/14 x3 ~2s exit0 watchdog-never-fires + fail-copy exit1. Requires 2 green CI runs to accept. FINAL ROOT CAUSE (surfaced by the observability add): after the hang was fixed, #310 still exited 1 — the gate's new FAIL-tail print revealed an AssertionError at external-research-live.test.ts:76 'time limit enforced ... status 0': the toEarly fetch used a 1ms timeout against an INSTANT in-process loopback server, so on a fast CI runner the response completed before 1ms ⇒ status 200 ⇒ flaky. This racy assertion was previously MASKED by the hang. FIX: time-limit enforcement is now DETERMINISTIC — a dedicated server that delays its response 3000ms vs a 100ms fetch deadline, so the deadline always trips ⇒ status 0; the slow server's timer is cleared on socket close and torn down with the can't-hang teardown. ALSO shipped (observability, odg-test-report.ts): the classified gate now prints a bounded stdout tail for FAIL/BLOCKED suites (the assertion error / ##SUITE_WATCHDOG dump) instead of only the suite name — which is what made this diagnosable; gate self-test 61/61. Local external-research-live 14/14 ×5 ~2s exit0 watchdog-never-fires; full gate green. Components: (1) httpGetBounded resolve-once [prod], (2) suite-exit watchdog [determinism+diagnostic], (3) gate FAIL-tail observability, (4) deterministic time-limit assertion [flaky-test fix]. 2 green CI runs required to accept. ACCEPTED: merged PR#310 @e1b5733; two consecutive green CI runs on the final commit + independent verifier PASS; external-research-live CI flake closed (resolve-once + suite watchdog + gate FAIL-tail observability + deterministic time-limit assertion).

items.title: patch-executor applyUnifiedDiff: bound hunk-start to EOF (DoS: oversized hunk header -> OOM/stall in prefix-copy loop)
items.evidence: Recon-confirmed HIGH: applyUnifiedDiff derives hunkStart from the (tool/attacker-controllable) declared old-start line, then runs `while (orig < hunkStart) result.push(origLines[orig++])`. A header like `@@ -999999999,1 @@` against a short file pushes ~1e9 `undefined` entries => memory blowup / multi-second stall (DoS) before the per-line context check can fail. The existing `hunkStart < orig` check guards only the LOWER bound. Fix: one strictly-greater guard `if (hunkStart > origLines.length) throw ...` (a start past EOF cannot apply; `hunkStart === origLines.length` stays legal for an append-at-EOF hunk). The throw is caught by the executor's patch-level catch and recorded FAILED (blocks validation; nothing half-written). Tests: patch-executor.test.ts +5 (now 25): oversized hunk handled <10s, exit 0, recorded FAILED with 'past end of file', no APPLIED entry, target file unmutated; PLUS an append-at-EOF regression (hunkStart === line count) that must still APPLY. build:runtime + tsc(both) green; sibling suites patch-executor-governance-guard 13/13 + symlink-confinement 19/19 green; full gate 243/243.

items.title: nl-objective-gateway: abstain fail-closed on an uncovered-locale objective (close the non-EN/FR/AR under-classification fail-open + fairness gap)

items.title: ollama-provider loopbackGet response-size cap (parity with loopbackPost; bound unbounded local-daemon body)
items.evidence: Recon-confirmed LOW-MED dos. loopbackGet (used by detectOllama for /api/tags discovery) accumulated data += c with NO byte cap, while loopbackPost enforces a 2MB cap and the file header explicitly promises 'a bounded timeout + response-size cap'.
